newsitem.title: USA: Weekly jobless claims down in latest week.
newsitem.headline: Weekly jobless claims down in latest week.

text.p: The number of Americans claiming new unemployment benefits fell last week to the lowest level in more than six months, the government said Thursday.
The Labour Department said weekly jobless claims in the week ended Feb. 8 were down to 309,000, the lowest level since the week ended July 27, when they were at 294,000.
Wall Street economists had forecast initial jobless claims of 339,000 in the Feb. 8 week.
The four-week moving average, viewed by economists as a more accurate gauge of jobless trends, fell to 327,750 last week from a revised 330,750 the week before.
That put the moving average at its lowest level since the week ended Sept. 14, when it stood at 326,250.
The department said seven states reported decreases in claims exceeding 1,000 on an unadjusted basis in the week ended Feb. 1, the latest period for which that data were available.
Among the largest were Tennessee with 6,239 fewer jobless claims, Texas with 5,220, North Carolina with 4,467 and Georgia with 3,151.
Tennessee reported fewer layoffs in the construction, service, apparel and transportation equipment industries. Texas had fewer layoffs in the electrical equipment, trade and service industries.
North Carolina said it had fewer layoffs in the construction, food, apparel, chemical and electrical equipment industries. Georgia had fewer layoffs in the carpet industry.
Labour said five states reported increases in initial claims exceeding 1,000, unadjusted, in the Feb. 1 week.
They were California with 11,085 additional claims, Iowa with 1,572, Connecticut with 1,550, New York with 1,218 and Florida with 1,079.

California said its increase was due to a return to a five-day workweek after a shorter reporting period the previous week. It also reported layoffs in the construction and food industries, and in agriculture.
Florida had layoffs in the construction, trade and service industries, and in manufacturing. New York, Connecticut and Iowa provided no reason for the pickup in claims activity.
